title: Forget how to walk
simplified_paragraphs: 两千年以前，有一个燕国人，他没有自信，常常觉得什么都比别人差——别人的衣服更好看，别人的饭菜更好吃，别人站的样子坐的样子更高雅。他看见什么学什么，学习了很多东西，但是一件事都做不好。
他甚至觉得自己走路的样子太丑了，别人都在笑他。
他听说邯郸人走路的样子很美。
邯郸人走路的样子有多美呢？他不知道。这是他的心病，然后他就去邯郸学习走路了！
到了邯郸，他觉得真有意思。看见小孩走路活泼，他学；看见老人走路高雅，他学；看见女人走路美，他也学。不到半个月，他就忘了自己以前是怎么走路的，钱也用完了，只能爬着回去了。
邯郸学步，意思是只学习别人，没有学到别人好的东西，又忘了自己的优点。这是《庄子》里的故事。
traditional_paragraphs: 兩千年以前，有一個燕國人，他沒有自信，常常覺得什麼都比別人差——別人的衣服更好看，別人的飯菜更好吃，別人站的樣子坐的樣子更高雅。他看見什麼學什麼，學習了很多東西，但是一件事都做不好。
他甚至覺得自己走路的樣子太醜了，別人都在笑他。
他聽說邯鄲人走路的樣子很美。
邯鄲人走路的樣子有多美呢？他不知道。這是他的心病，然後他就去邯鄲學習走路了！
到了邯鄲，他覺得真有意思。看見小孩走路活潑，他學；看見老人走路高雅，他學；看見女人走路美，他也學。不到半個月，他就忘了自己以前是怎麼走路的，錢也用完了，只能爬著回去了。
邯鄲學步，意思是只學習別人，沒有學到別人好的東西，又忘了自己的優點。這是《莊子》裡的故事。

tā shèn zhì jué de zì jǐ zǒu lù de yàng zi tài chǒu le， bié rén dōu zài xiào tā。
tā tīng shuō Hán dān rén zǒu lù de yàng zi hěn měi。
Hán dān rén zǒu lù de yàng zi yǒu duō měi ne？ tā bù zhī dào。 zhè shì tā de xīn bìng， rán hòu tā jiù qù Hán dān xué xí zǒu lù le！

dào le Hán dān， tā jué de zhēn yǒu yì si。 kàn jiàn xiǎo hái zǒu lù huó pō， tā xué； kàn jiàn lǎo rén zǒu lù gāo yǎ， tā xué； kàn jiàn nǚ rén zǒu lù měi， tā yě xué。 bù dào bàn gè yuè， tā jiù wàng le zì jǐ yǐ qián shì zěn me zǒu lù de， qián yě yòng wán le， zhǐ néng pá zhe huí qù le。
Hán dān xué bù， yì si shì zhǐ xué xí bié rén， méi yǒu xué dào bié rén hǎo de dōng xi， yòu wàng le zì jǐ de yōu diǎn。 zhè shì《 Zhuāng zǐ》 lǐ de gù shi。
english_paragraphs: Two thousand years ago, there was a man from the state of Yan who lacked confidence. He often felt that he was worse than everyone else: other people’s clothes looked better, their food tasted better, and even the way they stood and sat seemed more elegant. He tried to copy everything he saw. He learned many things, but couldn’t do any of them well.
He even thought the way he walked was ugly and that everyone was laughing at him.
Then he heard that people in Handan walked beautifully.
How beautifully did they walk? He didn’t know, but the question kept bothering him. So he went to Handan to learn how to walk!

When he arrived in Handan, he found it fascinating. He saw children walking with a spring in their step, so he copied them. He saw old people walking elegantly, so he copied them too. He saw women walking gracefully, and he copied them as well. In less than two weeks, he had forgotten how he used to walk. He had also run out of money, so he had to crawl home.
The saying “learning to walk in Handan” means copying others without learning what is good about them, while forgetting your own strengths. This story comes from the Zhuangzi.
english_full:
Two thousand years ago, there was a man from the state of Yan who lacked confidence. He often felt that he was worse than everyone else: other people’s clothes looked better, their food tasted better, and even the way they stood and sat seemed more elegant. He tried to copy everything he saw. He learned many things, but couldn’t do any of them well.

He even thought the way he walked was ugly and that everyone was laughing at him.

Then he heard that people in Handan walked beautifully.

How beautifully did they walk? He didn’t know, but the question kept bothering him. So he went to Handan to learn how to walk!

When he arrived in Handan, he found it fascinating. He saw children walking with a spring in their step, so he copied them. He saw old people walking elegantly, so he copied them too. He saw women walking gracefully, and he copied them as well. In less than two weeks, he had forgotten how he used to walk. He had also run out of money, so he had to crawl home.

The saying “learning to walk in Handan” means copying others without learning what is good about them, while forgetting your own strengths. This story comes from the Zhuangzi.
